subject: general
question: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. F sits second to the right of G. F sits at one of the corners. Only three people sit between G and E when counted from the left of G. H sits third to the left of E. Only three people sit between H and B when counted from the left of H. C sits second to the right of B. D is not an immediate neighbour of E. How many people sit between E and D, when counted from the left of D?
solution:
A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table.

 
• Some of them are sitting at the corners while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides.
 
• F sits second to the right of G.
 
• F sits at one of the corners.
 
• Only three people sit between G and E when counted from the left of G.
 
• H sits
